_comment: Every numeric constant in the engine lives here, never inline in code.
Values marked (spec) are taken verbatim from the prototype spec; values
marked (product) are hypotheses this module had to choose because the spec
leaves them open. Spec section 11.1: 'The weights are product hypotheses,
not scientific truth. A qualified trade expert must review them.'
thresholds_version is embedded in every decision and in the idempotency
key, so changing any number here re-assesses rather than silently drifting.

score_weights._source: spec section 11.1 (must sum to 1.0 — asserted at import)

hard_rules._source: spec section 11.2 — these are NOT averaged away

media_quality._source: spec section 12.3 — award-if-at-least/at-most, weights sum to 1.0
_product_cutoffs: (product) Spec section 12.3 defines how media quality is scored but not
what counts as too poor to review. These two are this module's choice.
no_person_below is deliberately far stricter than
min_person_visible_ratio: barely-in-frame is a quality problem worth a
resubmission, whereas nobody in frame at all means there is no practical
evidence to assess and the outcome is insufficient_evidence instead.

_comment: (product) Spec section 11.4 names the five bands but gives no cutoffs.
Coverage gates come first: a high score computed from thin evidence is
exactly the misleading number spec section 11.3 warns about.

knowledge._comment: (product) low knowledge is a note, never an automatic fail — spec section 10.2 'Good video with low quiz score: mixed confidence; do not automatically fail'
